paragraphs: X Mtxs- afflicted, the deities, sages, and ascetics, wrought up with fear, sought the protection of that god of gods— Mahe?wara— creator and destroyer of the cosmos, — unborn, of an unmanifest form, the stay of all creatures, worthy of being adored,- and the supreme preceptor (of all). And coining to that enemy of Kama* and foe of Tripura — the three-eyed (Deity), the gods, with their voices faltering through fear, represented with joined hands, — ‘O reverend one, tlie creatures of the lord of creatures are being (sorely) troubled by the sons of Sukega, given to harassing their foes, — swolen with insolence on account of the boon conferred on tliem by the great-father. Our asylums,— constituting our refuges,— have been divested of their power of granting shelter; and driving off the deities from the etherial regions, they are sporting there like the immortals.

‘I am Vishnu,’ ‘I am Rudra,’ ‘I am the king of the celestials,’ ‘I am Yama,’ ‘I am Vanina,’ ‘I am the Moon,’ ‘I am the Sun,’ — flattering the fool-hardiness to disturb the contemplation of the former. By the way, Kfilidfisa has reared his faery fabric,entilled Kumira Sanibhava, On the basis of UTTJ RAKANDA M. themselves in this fashion, Mali and Sutnali and the Rakshasa — MaK avail — as well as those going before them, are annoying (the gods), breathing exhilaration of martial spirits. Therefore, O god, it behoveth thee to liberate us from fear, who have been greatly tormented by it. Do thou, assuming thy terrific form, slay the thorns of the celestials.’ Thus addressed by the immortals in a body, that lord, Kaparddi of rctl-blue hue, reflecting that it would be wrong for him to ilestroy Suke^a (with his own hands), spoke unto the gods, — ‘1 shall not slay them, ye gods ; they are incapable of being slain by me.

But I shall unfold unto you the way in which they w ill be destroyed. Do ye, ye Maharshis, in the heat of this affair, seek the shelter of Vishnu. That lord will slay them.’ Thereat, saluting Mahe 9 wara with the sounds of Java, (the celestials) afflicted with the fear of the nightrangers, presented Uiemselves before Vishnu. And bowing down unto the god holding the conch, discus and mace, and paying him high homage, they, greatly flurried, addressed him .about the .sons of Sukeya, saying,^ — ‘O god, by virtue of the boon (that hath been bestowed on them), resembling the three lires, Sukc^a’s three sons, assailing us, have deprived us of our abode. There is a city named Lanka, stationed on the lop of Trikuta, (extremely) difficult of entrance.

Taking up their station at that place, the night-rangers in a body pursue us. Do thou, O slayer of Madhu, destroy them for our welfare. We have .sought thy shelter. Become our refuge, O foremost of celestials. Do thou dedicate to Yama the lotuses of their faces, severed (in pieces) with thy discus. Save thcQ, we have none who can, while tormented with fright, inspire us with courage. Slay in encounter the elated Rakshasas along with their adherents ; and even as the sun drieth up dew, do thou dispell this fear of ours.’ Thus acco.sted by the deities, that god of gods — JanSrddana — who bringeth fear unto foes — cheering up the celestials, said unto them, — ‘I know the Rakshasa, Suke^a, as flushed with the RAMA YANA, boon bestowed by lyana.

And I also know his sons, of whom MalyavSn is the eldest. Those worst of RSksliasas that have over-riden your dignity will I, wrought up with wrath, slay (in battle) ; therefore, ye gods, be of good cheer.’ Thus addressed by the mighty Vishnu, the gods, highly rejoiced, went to their respective quarters, extolling JanSrdana. “And hearing of the activity of the celestials, the nightranger — Malyavan — addressed his heroic brothers, saying, — ‘The immortals and sages, going to Sankara, spake these words, desirous of our destruction, — Tlie terrific sons of Sukeqia, puffed up, and swollen on account of their strength flowing from the boon, are crossing us at every step. Wc have been overpowered by the Raksbasas, And, O lord of creatures, from fear of those wicked-minded ones, we cannot remain in our own homes.

Therefore, to do us good, do thou, O three-eyed one, destroy then:i ; and, O best of cor>suming ones, do thou with thy roars, burn them up. — Thus addressed by the deities, the slayer of Andhaka, bearing their speech, said, shaking his head and hands, — Ye gods, Suke^a’s sons arc incapable of being slain by me in battle. But I shall tell you the means wdiereby they may be slain. Do ye seek the shelter of him wiio holdcth the dkscus and mace in his hands, and who is clad in a yellow attire, — of Janardana, Hari, even of the auspicious Narayana.— Having received this counsel of Mara, they, rendering reverence unto that enemy of Kama, came to the abode of Narayana and communicated everything unto him.

Then Narayana spoke unto the celestials with Indra at their head, — I will slay those foes of the celestials. Ye gods, cast off all fear! — O foremost of Rakshasas, Ilari promised unto the frightened celestials that he would slay us. Therefore do ye think as to what is frt. Hiranyakat^'ipii hath met with death (at the hands of Hari), as also other enemies of the immortals. And Namuchi and Kaianerni, and that foremost of heroes, — Sanhrada — and Radheya, and Yahum§yi, and the virtuous Lokapala, and Y5mala, and UTTA RA KA NDA M. i57( J\rjuna, and Hardikyn, and Sumbha and Ni(;umbliaka, — Asuras and Danavas endowed with strength and possessed of terrific prowess — all these, who, having come to the field, had never been heard of as worsted, who had performed hundreds of sacrifices, who had been well skilled in illusion, who had been versed in every branch of knowledge, and who were the terrors of their foes — havo by hundreds and by thousands been destroyed by NarSyana.

Learning this, it behoveth you to do what would conduce to the behoof of all. It is a sore task to defeat Narayana, who wisheth to slay us.’ Thereat Sumali and M31i, hearing the words of Malyavan, said unto their eldest brother, like the Aqiwins addressing Vasava, — ‘We have studied, performed sacrifices, practised charity, and obtained riches ; and attaining long health and long life, we have established sterling righteousness in our path. And with arms plunging into the sea of celestials, we have conquered our unrivalled enemies. Therefore, we have no fear touching death. Even .NSrayana and Rudra, Sakra and Yama, ever fear to stay before us (in the field). And, O lord of R^kshasas, there is no occasion for Vishnu’s displeasure of us.

The mind of Vishnu hath wavered in consequence of the evil caused by the celestials. Therefore will we even avenge ourselves on the gods, from whom hath sprung this wrong.’ Having taken counsel together, those powerful ones conciliated their forces. And proclaiming (their order) that preparations were to be made, all the foremost Nairiias sallied forth for battle, like unto those led by Jamva and Vritra. And, O Rama, having thus taken counsel togo'tlier, with all the preparations complete, those hugebodied and redoubtable Rakshas marched forth for conflict, mounted on cars, and elephants, and horses resembling elcpliants, and mules, and kinc, and camels, and purpoiscs,* and serpents, makaras, and tortoises, and fishes, and fowls J57-J JRAJIIA I'AJVA. resembling Garura himself, lions and tigers and boars anti Sf'imaras* and Chdmaras.'^ And puffed up with pride of prowess, the Rakshas march, leaving Lanka, and the enemies of the celestials went to the heavenly regions for battle.

And perceiving the destruction of I^nka at hand, those deities that had taken up their quarters there, everywhere were struck with fear and felt their •spirits depressed. And mounting the best of cars, the Rakshasas by hundreds and thousands with intent minds swiftly sallied forth for the celestial regions. And the deities (aforementioned) followed the tract of the Rakshasas. And at the command of Kala, terrible evil omens foreshadowing the destruction of the Rakshasachiefs began to arise on the earth welt as in the sky. The clouds showered down bones and hot blood. The oceans overleapt their continents and the mountains shook. And jackals of terrific forms, having voices resembling the roaring of clouds, — bursting out into a horse-laugh, began to emit cries frightfully.

Creatures were one after another seen to drop down ; and mighty swarms of vultures, with mouths belching forth flames, began to wheel over the Rakshasa, like unto Kala himself. And blood-footed pigeons and Sarikas§ darted ofT (around). And crows and two-legged cats began to cry in loud accents. But fast bound with the noose of Death, the Rakshasas, proud of their strength, disregarding these omens, march on, and do not stay their course, — Malyavan and Sumali possessed of prodigious strength, going before the Rakshasas, like flaming fires. And even as the gods take refuge under Dhata, the night-rangers take refuge under Malyavan resembling the mountain, Malyavan. And under the command of Mali, that host ot t Bos Grunniens. t Used in the Shakespercan sense : Vide Macbeth. i A species of harlot. ^akshasas, roaring like mighty clouds, inspired with the desire of victory, went to the celestial regions.

And the lord NSrayana, hearing of the preparations of the Rakshasas from a celestial messenger, set his heart on fight. And equipped with weapons and quivers, he mounted on Vinata’s offspring * And donning on his mail furnished w’ith the effulgence of a thousand suns, fastening his spotless quivers filled with shafts, being engirt with his waist-band and bright falchion, and equipped with his conch, discus, mace, Sarnia, ^ sword, and other superior weapons, that lotus-eyed lord, seated on Vinata’s offspring like a very mountain, set out speedily for compassing the destruction of the RSkshasas. And seated on Suparna’sJ back, the blue-brown Hari clad in yellow attire resembled a mass of clouds on the crest of the golden mountain, with lightning playing through it.

And hymned by Siddhas and celestials and sages and mighty (semi-divine) serpents and Gandharvas and Yakhas, the enemy of the Asura hosts jM-esented himself, bearing in his hands the discus, sword, that weapon — Sdrnga — and the conch. And the Rakshasa-hosts, struck by the wind produced by the wings of Suparna, with their pennons swinging to and fro and their weapons scattered about, quaked like the blue summit of a mountain with its crags tossed about. Then the night-rangers, hemming in Madhava,§ began to pierce him with thousands of excellent sharpened weapons dyed in flesh and blood, and resembling the fire of Doomsday.” T The bow of Vishnu is so named. t \a\.. fair-feathcrcd — a name of Garura. t Oitc of the many designations of Vishnu. liAMA FAJVA.

verses.sa:
तैर्वध्यमाना देवाश्च ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः ।
भयार्ताः शरणं जग्मुर्देवदेवं महेश्वरम् ॥

जगत्सृष्ट्यन्तकर्तारमजमव्यक्तरूपिणम् ।
आधारं सर्वलोकानामाराध्यं परमं गुरुम् ॥

ते समेत्य तु कामारिं त्रिपुरारिं त्रिलोचनम् ।
ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयो देवा भयगद्गदभाषिणः ॥

सुकेशपुत्रैर्भगवन्पितामहवरोद्धतैः ।
प्रजाध्यक्ष प्रजाः सर्वा बाध्यन्ते रिपुबाधनैः ॥

शरण्यान्यशरण्यानि ह्याश्रमाणि कृतानि नः ।
स्वर्गाच्च देवान्प्रच्याव्य स्वर्गे क्रीडन्ति देववत् ॥

अहं विष्णुरहं रुद्रो ब्रह्माहं देवराडहम् ।
अहं यमश्च वरुणश्चन्द्रो ऽहं रविरप्यहम् ॥

इति माली सुमाली च माल्यवांश्चैव राक्षसाः ।
बाधन्ते समरोद्धर्षा ये च तेषां पुरःसराः ।
तन्नो देव भयार्तानामभयं दातुमर्हसि ॥
अशिवं वपुरास्थाय जहि वै देवकण्टकान् ॥

धन्ते समरोद्धर्षा ये च तेषां पुरःसराः ।
इत्युक्तस्तु सुरैः सर्वैः कपर्दी नीललोहितः ।
सुकेशं प्रति सापेक्षः प्राह देवगणान्प्रभुः ॥

अहं तान्न हनिष्यामि मयावध्या हि ते सुराः ।
किं तु मन्त्रं प्रदास्यामि यो वै तान्निहनिष्यति ॥

एतमेव समुद्योगं पुरस्कृत्य महर्षयः ।
गच्छध्वं शरणं विष्णुं हनिष्यति स तान्प्रभुः ॥

ततस्तु जयशब्देन प्रतिनन्द्य महेश्वरम् ।
विष्णोः समीपमाजग्मुर्निशाचरभयार्दिताः ॥

शङ्खचक्रधरं देवं प्रणम्य बहुमान्य च ।
ऊचुः सम्भ्रान्तवद्वाक्यं सुकेशतनयान्प्रति ॥

सुकेशतनयैर्देव त्रिभिस्त्रेताग्निसन्निभैः ।
आक्रम्य वरदानेन स्थानान्यपहृतानि नः ॥

लङ्का नाम पुरी दुर्गा त्रिकूटशिखरे स्थिता ।
तत्र स्थिताः प्रबाधन्ते सर्वान्नः क्षणदाचराः ॥

स त्वमस्मद्धितार्थाय जहि तान्मधुसूदन ।
शरणं त्वां वयं प्राप्ता गतिर्भव सुरेश्वर ॥

चक्रकृत्तास्यकमलान्निवेदय यमाय वै ।
भयेष्वभयदो ऽस्माकं नान्यो ऽस्ति भवता विना ॥

राक्षसान्समरे दुष्टान्सानुबन्धान्मदोद्धतान् ।
नुदं त्वं नो भयं देव नीहारमिव भास्करः ॥

इत्येवं दैवतैरुक्तो देवदेवो जनार्दनः ।
अभयं भयदो ऽरीणां दत्त्वा देवानुवाच ह ॥

सुकेशं राक्षसं जाने ईशानवरदर्पितम् ।
तांश्चास्य तनयाञ्जाने येषां ज्येष्ठः स माल्यवान् ॥

तानहं समतिक्रान्तमर्यादान्राक्षसाधमान् ।
निहनिष्यामि सङ्क्रुद्धः सुरा भवत विज्वराः ॥

इत्युक्तास्ते सुराः सर्वे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ।
यथावासं ययुर्हृष्टाः प्रशंसन्तो जनार्दनम् ॥

विबुधानां समुद्योगं माल्यवांस्तु निशाचरः ।
श्रुत्वा तौ भ्रातरौ वीराविदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥

अमरा ऋषयश्चैव सङ्गम्य किल शकरम् ।
अस्मद्वधं परीप्सन्त इदं वचनमब्रुवन् ॥

सुकेशतनया देव वरदानबलोद्धताः ।
बाधन्ते ऽस्मान्समुद्दृप्ता घोररूपाः पदे पदे ॥

राक्षसैरभिभूताः स्म न शक्ताः स्म प्रजापते ।
स्वेषु सद्मसु संस्थातुं भयात्तेषां दुरात्मनाम् ॥

तदस्माकं हितार्थाय जहि तांश्च त्रिलोचन ।
राक्षसान्हुङ्कृतेनैव दह प्रदहतां वर ॥

इत्येवं त्रिदशैरुक्तो निशम्यान्धकसूदनः ।
शिरः करं च धुन्वान इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥

अवध्या मम ते देवाः सुकेशतनया रणे ।
मन्त्रं तु वः प्रदास्यामि यस्तान्वै निहनिष्यति ॥

यो ऽसौ चक्रगदापाणिः पीतवासा जनार्दनः ।
हरिर्नारायणः श्रीमान् शरणं तं प्रपद्यथ ॥

हरादवाप्य ते मन्त्रं कामारिमभिवाद्य च ।
नारायणालयं प्राप्य तस्मै सर्वं न्यवेदयन् ॥

ततो नारायणेनोक्ता देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः ।
सुरारींस्तान्हनिष्यामि सुरा भवत विज्वराः ॥

देवानां भयभीतानां हरिणा राक्षसर्षभौ ।
प्रतिज्ञातो वधो ऽस्माकं चिन्त्यतां यदिह क्षमम् ॥

हिरण्यकशिपोर्मृत्युरन्येषां च सुरद्विषाम् ।
नमुचिः कालनेमिश्च संह्रादो वीरसत्तमः ॥

राधेयो बहुमायी च लोकपालो ऽथ धार्मिकः ।
यमलार्जुनौ च हार्दिक्यः शुम्भश्चैव निशुम्भकः ॥

असुरा दानवाश्चैव सत्त्ववन्तो महाबलाः ।
सर्वे समरमासाद्य न श्रूयन्ते ऽपराजिताः ॥

सर्वैः क्रतुशतैरिष्टं सर्वे मायाविदस्तथा ।
सर्वे सर्वास्त्रकुशलाः सर्वे शत्रुभयङ्कराः ॥

नारायणेन निहताः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ।
एतज्ज्ञात्वा तु सर्वेषां क्षमं कर्तुमिहार्हथ ॥

ततः सुमाली माली च श्रुत्वा माल्यवतो वचः ।
ऊचतुर्भ्रातरं ज्येष्ठं भगांशाविव वासवम् ॥

स्वधीतं दत्तमिष्टं चाप्यैश्वर्यं परिपालितम् ।
आयुर्निरामयं प्राप्तं सुधर्मः प्रापितः पथि ॥

देवसागरमक्षोभ्यं शस्त्रैः समवगाह्य च ।
जिता द्विषो ह्यप्रतिमास्तन्नो मृत्युकृतं भयम् ॥

नारायणश्च रुद्रश्च शक्रश्चापि यमस्तथा ।
अस्माकं प्रमुखे स्थातुं सर्वे बिभ्यति सर्वदा ॥

विष्णोर्देवस्य नास्त्येव कारणं राक्षसेश्वर ।
देवानामेव दोषेण विष्णोः प्रचलितं मनः ॥

तस्मादद्य समुद्युक्ताः सर्वसैन्यसमावृताः ।
देवानेव जिघांसाम एभ्यो दोषः समुत्थितः ॥

एवं सम्मन्त्र्य बलिनः सर्वे सैन्यसमावृताः ।
उद्योगं घोषयित्वा तु सर्वे नैर्ऋतपुङ्गवाः ।।
युद्धाय निर्ययुः क्रुद्धा जम्भवृत्रबला इव ॥

इति ते राम सम्मन्त्र्य सर्वोद्योगेन राक्षसाः ।
युद्धाय निर्ययुः सर्वे महाकाया महाबलाः ॥

स्यन्दनैर्वारणैश्चैव हयैश्च गिरिसन्निभैः ।
खरैर्गोभी रथोष्ट्रैश्च शिंशुमारैर्भुजङ्गमैः ॥

मकरैः कच्छपैर्मीनैर्विहङ्गैर्गरुडोपमैः ।
सिंहैर्व्याघ्रैर्वराहैश्च सृमरैश्चमरैरपि ॥

त्यक्त्वा लङ्कां गताः सर्वे राक्षसा बलगर्विताः ।
प्रयाता देवलोकाय योद्धुं दैवतशत्रवः ॥

लङ्काविपर्ययं दृष्ट्वा यानि लङ्कालयान्यथ ।
भूतानि भयदर्शीनि विमनस्कानि सर्वशः ॥
रथोत्तमैरुह्यमानाः शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ॥

प्रयाता राक्षसास्तूर्णं देवलोकं प्रयत्नतः ।
रक्षसामेव मार्गेण दैवतान्यपचक्रमुः ॥

भौमाश्चैवान्तरिक्षाश्च कालाज्ञप्ता भयावहाः ।
उत्पाता राक्षसेन्द्राणामभावाय समुत्थिताः ॥

अस्थीनि मेघा ववृषुरुष्णं शोणितमेव च ।
वेलां समुद्राश्चोत्क्रान्ताश्चेलुश्चाप्यथ भूधराः ॥

अट्टहासान्विमुञ्चन्तो घननादसमस्वनाः ।
वाश्यन्त्यश्च शिवास्तत्र दारुणं घोरदर्शनाः ॥

सम्पतन्त्यथ भूतानि दृश्यन्ते च यथाक्रमम् ।
गृध्रचक्रं महच्चात्र ज्वलनोद्गारिभिर्मुखैः ॥

राक्षसानामुपरि खे भ्रमते ऽलातचक्रवत् ।
कपोता रक्तपादाश्च शारिका विद्रुता ययुः ।।
काका वाश्यन्ति तत्रैव बिडाला वै द्विपादयः ॥

उत्पातांस्ताननादृत्य राक्षसा बलगर्विताः ।
यान्त्येव न निवर्त्तन्ते मृत्युपाशावपाशिताः ॥

माल्यवांश्च सुमाली च माली च सुमहाबलाः ।
आसन्पुरःसरास्तेषां क्रतूनामिव पावकाः ॥

माल्यवन्तं च ते सर्वे माल्यवन्तमिवाचलम् ।
निशाचरा ह्याश्रयन्ति धातारमिव देवताः ॥

तद्बलं राक्षसेन्द्राणां महाभ्रघननादितम् ।
जयेप्सया देवलोकं ययौ मालिवशे स्थितम् ॥

राक्षसानां समुद्योगं तं तु नारायणः प्रभुः ।
देवदूतादुपश्रुत्य चक्रे युद्धे तदा मनः ॥

स सज्जायुधतूणीरो वैनतेयोपरि स्थितः ।
आसज्ज्य कवचं दिव्यं सहस्रार्कसमद्युति ॥

आबध्य शरसम्पूर्णे इषुधी विमले तदा ।
श्रोणिसूत्रं च खड्गं च विमलं कमलेक्षणः ।।
शङ्खचक्रगदाशार्ङ्गखड्गाख्यप्रवरायुधान् ॥

सुपर्णं गिरिसङ्काशं वैनतेयमथास्थितः ।
राक्षसानामभावाय ययौ तूर्णतरं प्रभुः ॥

सुपर्णपृष्ठे स बभौ श्यामः पीताम्बरो हरिः ।
काञ्चनस्य गिरेः शृङ्गे सतडित्तोयदो यथा ॥

स सिद्धदेवर्षिमहोरगैश्च गन्धर्वयक्षैरुपगीयमानः ।
समाससादासुरसैन्यशत्रूंश्चक्रासिशार्ङ्गायुधशङ्खपाणिः ॥

सुपर्णपक्षानिलनुन्नपक्षं भ्रमत्पताकं प्रविकीर्णशस्त्रम् ।
चचाल तद्राक्षसराजसैन्यं चलोपलं नील इवाचलेन्द्रः ॥

ततः शरैः शोणितमांसरूषितैर्युगान्तवैश्वानरतुल्यविग्रहैः ।
निशाचराः सम्परिवार्य माधवं वरायुधैर्निर्बिभिदुः सहस्रशः ॥
